company.name: Mowi ASA
company.summary: Mowi ASA, a seafood company, produces and sells Atlantic salmon products worldwide. It operates through Feed, Farming, Markets, Consumer Products, and other segments. The company is involved in salmon feed production, salmon farming and primary processing, and seafood secondary processing activities. It offers whole fish, plain and marinated fillets and steaks, hot- and cold-smoked salmon, and burgers and patties, as well as breaded, gravad, and sushi products. The company was formerly known as Marine Harvest ASA and changed its name to Mowi ASA in December 2018. Mowi ASA was founded in 1964 and is based in Bergen, Norway.

caveats: An oil beta is co-movement with a sign, not causation: Brent moves for demand as well as supply reasons.
Outside energy most of the oil beta is a demand-shock beta — it reflects the news that moved oil, not the oil price.
The interval covers uncertainty about the expected move only. P(same sign) is how often the move actually goes that way.
Estimated on a universe of today's listings, so delisted companies are missing (survivorship).
oil_sensitivity.method: r = a + b_mkt*index + b_oil*Brent on Friday-to-Friday log returns, Newey-West standard errors; the total beta orthogonalises the index against oil first, so it is the effect through every channel

narrative.company_subtitle: Mowi ASA – Farm Products in Norway
narrative.company_headline: 5.0% revenue CAGR, 20.9% EBITDA margin and 2.2x net debt/EBITDA — market cap EUR 9.4bn
highlights: **Consistent growth:** revenue compounded at 5.0% p.a. over 2022–2025, reaching EUR 5,689m
**Margin profile:** pre-IFRS 16 EBITDA margin of 20.9% in 2025A (down from 24.9% in 2022A), EBIT margin 16.5%
**Cash generative:** unlevered FCF of EUR 634m in 2025A, 53% of EBITDA, ROIC 11%
**Balance sheet:** net debt of EUR 2,826m equals 2.2x EBITDA, a moderate leverage level
narrative.market_subtitle: Mowi versus its peer group: growth, profitability and the drivers behind the case
narrative.market_headline: Peer benchmarking on a consistent basis
opportunities: **Growth runway:** consensus expects 11.6% revenue growth in 2026E
**Operating leverage:** every 1pp of EBITDA margin is worth roughly EUR 80m of EBITDA in 2031E
disruption: **Business model shifts** in the sector may change the competitive set
threats: **Macro:** consumer spending, interest rates and FX can move revenue and the discount rate simultaneously
financial_commentary: **Mowi grew revenue by 2.2% in 2025A** to EUR 5,689m, with pre-IFRS 16 EBITDA of EUR 1,189m (20.9% margin)
**We forecast 2026E revenue of EUR 6,350m (+11.6%)**, anchored on consensus (9 analysts), fading to 2.0% terminal growth by 2031E
**EBITDA margin path:** 20.8% in 2026E to 20.1% in 2031E; D&A 4.1% and capex 6.9% normalising to 4.3% of revenue; tax rate 22%
**Unlevered FCF** rises from EUR 323m to EUR 909m over the forecast period (11.3% FCF margin in 2031E)
**Valuation vs peers:** Mowi trades at 10.4x LTM EV/EBITDA versus a peer median of 11.2x (-8%) and 14.7x P/E versus 33.0x
**Street view:** consensus target of NOK 224.40 across 11 analysts (+16% vs current price)
narrative.valuation_subtitle: We recommend a BUY. Our 12-month target price of NOK 308.50 implies +59% upside and a +63% total return including dividend; 9.4x 2026E EV/EBITDA.
narrative.valuation_headline: DCF fair value NOK 293.47, peer multiples NOK 203.35, scenario-weighted NOK 303.68 versus a share price of NOK 193.70 — BUY
market_implied: **Market-implied WACC 8.3%**, above our 6.6%: the price discounts our cash flows at 170bp more than we do
**Market-implied margin:** at our WACC the price is consistent with a 2031E EBITDA margin of 16.2% versus 20.1% in our base case

**Cross-check – low agreement:** the DCF is 44% above the peer-multiple value (NOK 203.35) and our target is 37% above the consensus of 11 analysts (NOK 224.40); the recommendation rests on the DCF assumptions alone — treat the target as a hypothesis, not a result
scenario_commentary: **Bear (25%):** Growth 2pp lower, margin 1.5pp lower, WACC +50bp; revenue CAGR 3.9%, 2031E margin 18.6%, WACC 7.1% gives NOK 208.01 (+7% vs price)
**Base (50%):** Base-case drivers; revenue CAGR 5.9%, 2031E margin 20.1%, WACC 6.6% gives NOK 293.47 (+52% vs price)
**Bull (25%):** Growth 2pp higher, margin 1.5pp higher, WACC -50bp; revenue CAGR 7.9%, 2031E margin 21.6%, WACC 6.1% gives NOK 419.78 (+117% vs price)
thesis: **DCF value of NOK 293.47 per share** (WACC 6.6%, terminal growth 2.0%); terminal value is 83% of EV, implying 12.5x exit EV/EBITDA
**Peer multiples imply NOK 203.35** per share (median of EV/EBITDA, EV/EBIT and P/E-based values)
**Scenarios:** bear NOK 208 / base NOK 293 / bull NOK 420; probability-weighted NOK 303.68
**12-month target price NOK 308.50:** fair value NOK 293.47 (valued at 23.09.2026) rolled forward at the 7.7% cost of equity less NOK 7.60 dividend; expected total return +63%, rating BUY
multiples_commentary: **Trading at a discount:** 10.4x EV/EBITDA vs 11.2x peer median (8% discount)
**Earnings multiple:** 14.7x trailing P/E vs 33.0x for peers (-55%); 13.6x vs 12.7x on next-twelve-month consensus
**Versus own history:** 10.4x trailing EV/EBITDA is above the 3.5-year median of 9.1x (64% of weeks were cheaper)
**EV/EBITDA-implied value:** NOK 215.15 at the peer median of 11.2x (range 192–253 across the 25th–75th percentile)
risks: **Oil price:** no measurable direct exposure — the share has moved +0.03% per 1% move in Brent over the last 5 years, an interval of -0.04 to +0.09 that spans zero (260 weeks to 2026-09-11); a higher oil price has been a cost: holding the index fixed, the share has moved -0.12% per 1% move in Brent
**Leverage:** net debt of 2.2x EBITDA limits flexibility if margins compress
**Value drivers:** WACC ±0.5pp moves fair value to NOK 257.2–338.5, terminal growth ±0.5pp to NOK 263.3–330.9 (base NOK 293.47)
**Execution:** the case assumes 11.6% growth in 2026E and margins of 20.1% by 2031E; a return to the 2022–2025 average margin of 21.3% would cut fair value
consensus: **EPS 2026E NOK 15.28 vs consensus NOK 12.50 (+22%):** we are above the 9 analysts – outside the range of estimates; 2027E +10%; our view rests on a 20.8% 2026E EBITDA margin and a 22% tax rate
**Revenue 2026E EUR 6,350m vs consensus EUR 6,385m (-0.6%):** in line by construction – our growth is anchored on consensus, so the differentiated view sits in margins
**Estimate momentum negative:** consensus EPS over the last 90 days 2026E -7.3%, 2027E -16.4%; 2 upward and 6 downward revisions in the last 30 days
**Tension:** our BUY runs against falling consensus estimates – shares rarely re-rate before revisions turn, so the timing of the case depends on the next reports
multiples_depth: **On next-twelve-month consensus** Mowi trades at 13.6x P/E (peers 12.7x), 1.8x EV/Sales (peers 1.7x), 9.4x EV/EBITDA at the LTM margin (peers 9.6x); PEG 0.71 vs 0.38

**Growth and margin explain 1% of the dispersion in peer EV/EBITDA** (4 peers): fundamentals justify 11.6x against the 11.2x median (+3%); the actual 10.4x leaves -11% unexplained. Evidence weak: multiples in this group are set by something the regression does not see – leverage, geography, liquidity or the cycle
**Cash and payout:** 3.1% levered FCF yield vs -0.2% for peers; 3.9% dividend yield vs 1.9%
**Consensus EPS growth FY1:** +19% for Mowi vs +39% for the peer median – the growth the forward multiple is buying
